rights._comment: AUTHORIZED OVERRIDE of rule 5's neutral-voice default (human-approved 2026-08-07): the company owns/authorizes its source content, so new projects default to voice CLONING ON with voice_clone_consent auto-recorded at init, and rights_status pre-set to a distributable value. This is NOT a silent bypass — consent is written through the sanctioned `rights set` CLI path (rule 1), the /new-video interview offers a one-click Neutral-voice opt-out (`--no-clone`), and a human can still revise at the human-only `rights-check` gate. Set default_voice_clone:false here (or in company.local.json) to restore the rule-5 neutral default company-wide. The three outward-facing disable-model-invocation skills (rights-check, video-release-authorize, video-promote-approve) keep their human-only posture regardless.

quality_bars._comment_audio: CONSTANT AUDIO SPEED is now a HARD RULE (TASK 2 / rule 5): dubbed audio is NEVER time-stretched to fit a caption slot — every cue plays at its natural TTS length and the PICTURE is re-timed (freeze/trim) around it. Picture re-timing is therefore MANDATORY, not opt-in: `dub run` always writes a per-language freeze plan and `package mux` always rebuilds the picture from it. `max_time_stretch`/`freeze_stretch_cap`/`freeze_frame_enabled` are retained for reporting/back-compat and are NO LONGER read to gate audio speed. `freeze_trim_languages` still chooses Model A (freeze+trim → residual 0) vs Model B (hold-only, honest residual) per language.

translation_models._comment: Fixed priority-language model policy (2026-08-10). The TRANSLATION fan-out (rule 16) drafts each track by language: a PRIORITY language uses `priority_model` (Opus-4.8/high), every other target uses `default_model` (Sonnet-5/high). No verify pass, no escalation, no tracking — a language is either priority or it isn't. en/ar/ur are the priority (most-important) editions; the rest (zh/fr/es/pt/ru/…) render on Sonnet. An explicit operator `dub`/translate model override still wins. Tune the list here or in company.local.json.

dubbing._comment: Male voice is the HARD default for EVERY language (TASK 2). `dub run`/autopilot auto-select `voices[<lang>][<gender>]` with no --model needed; an explicit `dub run --model` still overrides. The per-project gender is chosen at `/new-video` (project.yaml dubbing.voice_gender, default male) and only overridden to female by an explicit human decision (e.g. a female source voice recorded at LANGUAGE_ID). Voice `.onnx` paths are machine-specific — put the real absolute paths in the gitignored company.local.json (which deep-merges over this); keep this file as the shape + policy. Missing gender for a lang => `dub run` fails with a stage-a-voice message rather than silently using the wrong gender. EXCEPTION: languages in `clone_languages` below do NOT use this gender registry at all.
dubbing._clone_comment: `clone_languages` are ALWAYS dubbed via XTTS voice-CLONE off the source speaker's audio (source/audio.wav), NOT the piper gender registry — so the male/female gender axis does NOT apply to them. `dub run --language <one of these>` with no --model auto-resolves to provider=xtts + clone (as if --clone were passed): it is consent-gated (requires rights voice_clone_consent=true, rule 5), needs the XTTS `tts` engine installed and a clone reference present, and FAILS LOUD if any is missing (never a silent piper fallback). An explicit `dub run --model <path>` or `--gender <g>` still overrides (auto-clone only fires when --model is unset). This is the company source of truth for clone-vs-piper; the `tts.per_language` map in tools.default.json only chooses the engine for an otherwise-unresolved provider. Tune this list here or in company.local.json.

budget.note: Vendor (billed) TTS providers are refused until a human raises vendor_spend_ceiling_usd above the running total in budget/ledger.json (company.local.json override). Local engines (kokoro/piper/xtts/chatterbox) are never spend-guarded.
